req.title: Update requires title
req.statement: The system shall render 'Title is required.' when POST /<id>/update omits the title.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/update must render 'Title is required.' when the title field is omitted or empty. Tests cover: (1) positive — valid update with title succeeds (EP, confirms the happy path and that the validation branch is not always triggered); (2) negative — POST with empty title returns 200 with 'Title is required.' in body (NEG + EP, directly targets the requirement); (3) boundary — POST with title='' (zero-length string, the exact boundary that triggers the error) vs title='A' (one character, the minimum valid title that should NOT trigger the error) (BVA); (4) decision-table — POST with title field entirely absent from form data (DT, different code path from empty string but same semantic); (5) state-transition — user must be logged in; unauthenticated request redirects to login instead of showing the error (STC). All tests use pre-loaded data: post id=2 belongs to user Rahul (id=1, password='stone').

tests.name: test_update_with_valid_title_redirects
preconditions: Post id=2 exists and belongs to user Rahul (id=1)
User Rahul is authenticated via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /2/update with title='Updated Title', body='Updated body'
expected: HTTP 302 redirect (successful update, no validation error)
Response body does NOT contain 'Title is required.'
trace: R-FLASKR-018: when title is provided, no error is shown — confirms the positive branch
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_update_with_valid_title_redirects():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': 'Updated Title', 'body': 'Updated body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert b'Title is required.' not in r.data

test_update_with_valid_title_redirects()

tests.name: test_update_unauthenticated_redirects_to_login
preconditions: No user is logged in (fresh client, no session)
actions: POST /2/update with title='', body='body' WITHOUT logging in first
expected: Response body does NOT contain 'Title is required.' (auth guard fires before validation)
trace: R-FLASKR-018: STC — unauthenticated state; login_required decorator redirects before title validation runs
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_update_unauthenticated_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    # No login — send POST directly
    r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': '', 'body': 'body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert '/auth/login' in r.headers['Location']
    assert b'Title is required.' not in r.data

from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_update_error_message_exact_text():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': '', 'body': 'body'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    # Exact string match — catches mutations to the error constant
    assert b'Title is required.' in r.data
    # Confirm the weaker variant without period is NOT what we rely on
    assert b'Title is required' in r.data  # subset also present
    # Confirm no redirect happened
    assert r.status_code != 302
